readers.why: this is the ONLY read that produces feed rows: `poll_events`, webhook_delivery.dispatch_pending, why_snapshot and change_feed all page through it. SQL-shaped (an indexed range scan), not a graph capability.
a dedupe probe before the CREATE; a unique index answers it. The same statement is also `_event_row_exists` below, so this row requires BOTH occurrences.

snippets: GRAPH.CONSTRAINT CREATE tortoise_ge_uid UNIQUE NODE GraphEvent
readers.needs: DDL: a uniqueness constraint on event_id
readers.why: the belt behind the dedupe pre-check (the app-side probe is the suspenders). ⚠️ Issued through `g.query()` inside a `try/except` that only logs, so it does not raise the reader — and on the server this was measured against it was REFUSED while the `event_id` exact-match index was present and installed: `ResponseError: missing supporting exact-match index` (`measurement-payload88.json`). FalkorDB builds the index asynchronously, so a constraint issued immediately after its index can fail for that reason; that `installed` flag in the measurement records "the command did not raise", NOT "the index is usable". Production runs on the app-side probe either way.
the index `read_after`'s ordered scan plans against.
#9208's loss discriminator: asks whether a failed append landed. Shares its statement text with the dedupe probe above, which is why the two rows both require TWO occurrences in the file.

the export carries `:GraphEvent` rows because it carries everything; it names no label and needs no capability. ⚠️ It is censused because a re-home must decide what the export does with the shape, not because it reads one.
the second whole-graph scan: the same statement shape as the line above, in the restore path, so both rows require TWO occurrences.

verdict: no reader needs a graph capability — every reader is a key lookup, an ordered range scan, an aggregate, a predicate delete, or the schema those three depend on
